# Legislation inventory: what the repository holds at each tier

*Generated by `alicia/scripts/legislation_inventory.py` on 6 November 2026. Phase A of the [legislation-links plan](plan_legislation_links.md) (DECISIONS E-116). Counts are from the files; the register checks are as on 6 November 2026. Everything in the register is an AI-assisted draft, not yet checked by a person.*

## Summary

- **Commonwealth and states are partly covered; councils not at all.** The register holds 255 items with 278 instruments, all Commonwealth, state or territory (0 council items). The 61 regimes name councils as a tier in 11 regimes, as one party each, with no council laws, bodies or planning terms behind them.
- **The register was built to evaluate reforms, not to list every law.** Items were chosen as reforms and settings that matter for competition, so they are a sample of the statute book, not an inventory of it. No list of all laws in force exists yet at any tier.
- **Few instruments can be traced to a register entry.** 115 of 278 instruments (41%) carry a register ID or link. The rest are titles only.
- **The industry coding is at the right level.** 469 of 560 industry codes on register items are classes. Regimes use class codes for most industry-specific coverage, but some map a whole class where a law covers part of it (pharmacy rules on all of 4271).
- **State versions are uneven.** Of 45 regimes whose rules differ by state, 9 have a register item in all eight states and territories, 11 in some, and 25 in none.
- **The regimes' evidence is mostly guidance.** 63 of 87 sources for the regime descriptions are business.gov.au pages, with the Productivity Commission next. Both are good for what a business deals with, but neither is the law itself.
- **Reusable machinery exists.** The register adapters read dates for a named law from the Federal Register and six state and territory registers. They need extending to list every law in force, and NSW (and possibly SA) needs another source.

## 2. Regimes: who does what, by tier

`regulation-register/regimes/`: 61 regimes (7 cross-cutting, 54 industry-specific). Each layer is one function performed by one tier of government.

| Tier | sets-rules | licenses | approves | inspects | collects | funds | Layers | Layers naming no body |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commonwealth | 16 | 21 | 9 | 16 | 2 | 4 | 68 | 28 of 68 |
| State or territory | 14 | 45 | 9 | 29 | 6 | 1 | 104 | 89 of 104 |
| Council |  | 2 | 7 | 4 |  | 1 | 14 | 14 of 14 |

Regimes with a council layer (11): Accommodation premises; Building licensing, approvals and the building code; Environment protection licences and approvals; Food safety; Hairdressing, beauty and skin penetration; Heavy vehicle registration, access and safety; Liquor licensing; Native vegetation and land clearing; Planning and development approval; Telecommunications, broadcasting and online services; Waste management and levies.

Issues: 55 evidenced issues, 3 of them tagged as varying council by council.

Reuse: regimes stay as the grouping a business sees, and each requirement in the new tables belongs to one. Their class maps become hypotheses to test against the laws (phase B). Their council layers say where council laws must be looked for in phase E.

## 3. State versions of regimes that differ by state

Of 45 regimes whose rules differ between states (state laws, model laws adopted with variations, or licences recognised across states), the number of the eight states and territories with a register item:

- **All eight (9):** Building licensing, approvals and the building code; Electrical, plumbing and gas licensing and equipment safety; Hairdressing, beauty and skin penetration; Motor vehicle dealers and repairers; Passenger transport accreditation; Payroll tax; Planning and development approval; Security industry licensing; Work health and safety.
- **Some (11):** Accommodation premises (3); Container deposits and packaging (7); Conveyancing and land titles (5); Electricity and gas market regulation (7); Fuel retailing (6); Gambling and wagering (2); Heavy vehicle registration, access and safety (6); Legal profession (3); Liquor licensing (5); Pharmacy ownership, premises and PBS approval (6); Retail trading hours (4).
- **None (25):** Agricultural and veterinary chemicals; Animal welfare and livestock; Biosecurity; Commercial agents and debt collectors; Environment protection licences and approvals; Film, game and publication classification; Fisheries and aquaculture; Food safety; Hazardous chemicals and dangerous goods; Home warranty insurance; Labour hire licensing; Mandatory product standards and labelling; Mining and petroleum titles and approvals; Native vegetation and land clearing; Primary production food safety and export controls; Property agents and residential tenancies; Security of payment in construction; Therapeutic goods and poisons; Tobacco and vape sales; Veterinary registration and premises; Waste management and levies; Water access and use; Water and sewerage utility regulation; Workers' compensation; Working with children checks.

Reuse: the 'all eight' regimes are the pattern for phase D; the others show where state laws have not been collected yet.

Industry-specific regimes that include a whole division (4): Customs, excise and trade; Environment protection licences and approvals; Hazardous chemicals and dangerous goods; Mining and petroleum titles and approvals. These need checking against the laws, since a division spans many activities.

The join key is ready: 506 classes and 4,440 ABS primary activities (`data/processed/anzsic/`), with 16 classes marked as mainly government, households or non-profit institutions serving households (`class_marks.csv`).

## 7. Reading the registers

The adapters in `alicia/src/alicia/legislation/` read dates for a law the register is asked about by name or ID. Listing every law in force is new work. Checks on 6 November 2026:

| Jurisdiction | Register | What the adapter reads | Reachable from here |
|---|---|---|---|
| CTH | Federal Register of Legislation: public REST API (no key) | Assent or making date, registration, repeal, commencement table, compilations | API answers lookups by name and ID; the in-force filter on all titles returned an error |
| NSW | NSW Legislation | Nothing: blocks automated requests | Refused (403); NSW Parliament's site also refused |
| VIC | Victorian Legislation | In-force version dates only | Home page loaded |
| QLD | Queensland Legislation | As-made XML; legislative history XML | Home page loaded |
| WA | WA Legislation | Act page (assent); history table | Home page loaded |
| SA | SA Legislation | Nothing: blocked in October 2026 | Home page loaded without a challenge; lists not yet tested. Official XML update packages on data.sa.gov.au (fortnightly) |
| TAS | Tasmanian Legislation | Amendment commencement table (JSON); as-made XML | Home page loaded |
| ACT | ACT Legislation Register | Notified date; commencement table | Home page loaded |
| NT | NT Legislation | As-assented page | Home page loaded |

| Other source | What it is | Status |
|---|---|---|
| AustLII | Free legal information institute (not official) | Refused (Cloudflare block) |
| Open Australian Legal Corpus (Isaacus, v7.1.0) | CC BY 4.0; in-force statutes and regulations of CTH, NSW, Qld, WA, SA, Tas as at 10 March 2025, with each law's official register URL | Dataset card read; corpus not downloaded |
| ABLIS (business.gov.au) | Licences and obligations by ANZSIC activity, jurisdiction, tier and council area; API needs a key | Site and public API documents read; key applied for by the owner |

## 9. What carries into phase B

- **Reuse as they are:** the class list and marks, the bodies, the regime groupings and issues, and the Federal Register adapter.
- **Reuse as starting points:** register instruments (seeds for the catalogue), regime class maps (hypotheses to test), and the state adapters (to extend from one law to all laws).
- **To fix in the new tables:** every instrument needs a register ID; links that cover part of a class are qualified with ABS primary activities; and industry-specific regimes coded to a whole division are checked.
- **New:**
  - a catalogue of every law in force at each tier;
  - councils as bodies, with their local laws;
  - a crosswalk from classes to each state's planning land-use terms;
  - a source for NSW (D2), and ABLIS for the completeness check (D3).
